Meta.title: Rizq — The pricing benchmark for Saudi freelancers
Meta.description: Price with confidence. Earn your rizq. — A real Saudi-market pricing benchmark, built on local data, so you know what to charge before you bid.

Hero.tagline: Price with confidence. Earn your rizq.
Hero.subtitle: The first Saudi-market pricing benchmark built on real local data. Know your fair rate before you send the next proposal.

HowItWorks.heading: Three steps to a fair price.
HowItWorks.subheading: No spreadsheets, no guesswork. Just real numbers from the Saudi freelance market.
HowItWorks.step1Body: From graphic design to web development, choose the specialty that matches your service.
HowItWorks.step2Body: Riyadh is not Jeddah. A beginner is not an expert. The details shape the number.
HowItWorks.step3Body: You'll receive a precise price range built on data from real Saudi freelancers like you.

Pricing.heading: Start free. Upgrade when you're ready.
Pricing.subheading: No hidden fees. No annual commitments. Cancel anytime.
Pricing.halalNote: Halal. No riba. A service subscription only.

Faq.heading: What freelancers ask before they sign up.
Faq.q1: Where does Rizq's data come from?
Faq.a1: A blend: completed projects on Saudi platforms (Mostaql, Khamsat, Bahr), contributions from freelancers themselves, and rates posted in LinkedIn and X job listings. Every record is reviewed before it enters the benchmark.
Faq.a2: We always show the sample size honestly. If it's based on 12 freelancers, we'll tell you. Transparency matters more than claimed precision.
Faq.a3: We want you to try us. If we don't earn it, you cancel. An annual plan with a discount is on the way for those who already trust the product.
Faq.a4: Yes. All contributions are anonymized before they enter the public benchmark. We don't expose any freelancer's or client's identity. Compliant with the Saudi PDPL.
Faq.q5: How is Rizq different from Mostaql or Khamsat?
Faq.a5: Those platforms match freelancers with clients. Rizq tells you the fair price before you bid — on any platform, or for a direct client.
Faq.q6: Will there be a proposal generator?
Faq.a6: Yes — in v0.2. Right now we're focused on getting the benchmark right first. Join the waitlist to be among the first to know.
Faq.q7: Does Rizq support Saudi payment methods?
Faq.a7: Yes. Mada, Visa, Mastercard, and Apple Pay through a Sharia-compliant Saudi payment processor.

Founder.heading: Built by a Saudi who lived the problem.
Founder.body: I'm Ammar — a data analyst in banking and a former freelancer. I lived the question of "am I charging right?" for years. Rizq is what I wish existed when I started — a real benchmark built on Saudi data, with full transparency on where every number comes from.
Founder.name: Ammar Al-Hassani

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.intro: By accessing or using Rizq, you agree to these Terms. Read them carefully.
Terms.s1Body: Rizq is a data platform that offers indicative price ranges for freelance services in the Saudi market, based on aggregated and reviewed data. The ranges are market information — they are not professional advice or a guarantee of any actual price.
Terms.s2Body: You're responsible for the accuracy of your account information and for any activity that happens through it. Do not share your credentials. Automated or abusive use of Rizq is prohibited and may lead to account suspension.
Terms.s3Body: The free tier allows 3 queries per month. The Pro tier is a monthly subscription, cancellable at any time from your account settings. There is no interest (riba) in any payment flow. Payments are processed by a Saudi-compliant processor.
Terms.s4Body: You can cancel your subscription at any time and retain access until the end of the paid period. Refunds are available within the first 7 days of a subscription, pro-rated to time used.
Terms.s5Body: The Rizq trademark, content, and code belong to its founder. The dataset shown is part of Rizq's database and may not be republished commercially without permission.
Terms.s6Body: Rizq data is provided "as is". We're not responsible for business decisions based on it. Use your own professional judgment when pricing.
Terms.s7Body: We may update these terms from time to time. Material changes will be announced to your registered email.
Terms.s8Body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Disputes are resolved before the competent Saudi courts.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: We respect your privacy. This policy explains what we collect and why, in line with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).
Privacy.s1Body: Your email and an encrypted password, plus your name, preferred language, and city if you provide them. A log of your queries (specialty, city, returned range). Limited technical data (browser, timestamp) for security and analytics.
Privacy.s2Body: To operate the service, improve benchmark accuracy, prevent abuse, and contact you about important updates. We do not sell your data to any third party.
Privacy.s3Body: Only infrastructure providers (hosting, database, error tracking, analytics, email). All are bound by confidentiality and data-processing agreements.
Privacy.s4Body: You can ask what we store about you, correct it, delete it, or export a copy. Email us at the address below and we'll respond within 14 days.
Privacy.s5Body: We use a session cookie to keep you logged in, and optional analytics cookies to understand how the product is used. We do not use ad-tracking cookies.
Privacy.s6Body: Your data is stored in Supabase's Central-EU region. Passwords are stored encrypted; the Rizq team cannot read them.
Privacy.s7Body: Rizq is not directed at users under 18, and we do not knowingly collect their data.
Privacy.s8Body: For privacy questions or to exercise your rights, email us below.

Methodology.title: Rizq pricing methodology
Methodology.intro: I'm Ammar, the founder. This page explains where the numbers you see come from, how we compute them, and when we refuse to answer. The goal: use Rizq knowing exactly what we built it on — never trust us blindly.
Methodology.s1Body: Three primary sources: (a) Saudi freelancers who submitted real project prices with optional proof, (b) public data from Saudi platforms and government tenders, (c) Saudi-issued labor and wage indices. Every record carries its source, date, and a trust weight. We don't blend them into a single faceless number.
Methodology.s2Body: Records are bucketed by specialty × city × experience tier × project size. Within each bucket we compute three points: the minimum, the median (50th percentile), and the maximum. What you see is a real market range — not a softened average.
Methodology.s3Body: A mean is pulled around by outliers — one luxury project or one underpriced gig distorts it. The median says: half the market earns less, half earns more. That's the truer everyday-pricing signal. The min and max give you the full shape if you need it.
Methodology.s4Body: Every result shows "based on N Saudi freelancers". N matters: 5 records is our floor — under that we say "insufficient data" rather than guess. As N grows, the range narrows and confidence rises. We don't hide thin samples behind round numbers.
Methodology.s5Body: Today we don't account for: exact project complexity, individual freelancer reputation, client urgency, or your network signals. These move real prices — but they need a smarter engine, which we're building for the next version. For now: the range is market-wide, not personal.
Methodology.s6Body: Records older than 18 months are flagged and down-weighted. The Saudi market moves. "Market price" today isn't necessarily "market price" last year. The index updates continuously as new submissions come in.
Methodology.s7Body: Every contribution is hand-reviewed before it enters the public dataset. We reject incomplete or unrealistic records. This is slow — but it's the only way to protect the quality of every number after yours.
Methodology.s8Body: If you see a price that doesn't match your market, you'd compute it differently, or you have a data source to suggest — email me. Rizq gets sharper with every note.
